topic.title: Getting Started with Translation
topic.shortdesc: A hands-on walkthrough of the translation workflow using the Hydraulic Gear Pump sample project.

body.p: The steps below let you try the translation workflow end to end, from editing English content to publishing a multilingual deliverable.

li.p: Create a project from the Hydraulic Gear Pump sample - Create a new project and choose the Hydraulic Gear Pump sample template. See Projects for the full procedure. Take a moment to explore the project:

ul.li: It is already set up with an en/ folder for the English source and a per-language folder for each translation, the layout described in Choosing a Project Structure for Translation.
It contains a translation index that reflects the current state of the project.

It contains a multilingual DITA Map that includes all the DITA Maps for individual languages in separate key scopes, a publication called Gear Pump Multilingual and a PDF deliverable associated with it.

li.p: Make a change to one of the topics - Open one of the English topics in the visual editor and make a small edit, for example adding a new step. See Reviewing and Editing Files in the Visual Editor. Commit the change.

Run the translation in all supported languages - Start a new translation job. In the New Translation dialog, choose the Publication to translate and a Target language, optionally add free-form Instructions for the agent, then select Translate. Each job translates into one target language, so start one job per language you want to publish in. See Running an Incremental Translation for what happens while the job runs.

Follow the job and bring in the results - Each job appears as a card showing its progress; you can stop a running job from its card. When a job finishes, select Bring into workspace on the card to add its translated files to your workspace.
Review and commit the translated files - Review the translated files and the translation index that were added to your workspace, then commit them. See Reviewing Translations Before You Commit.

Publish the multilingual PDF - Open the project's Deliverables page and build the Gear Pump to Multilingual PDF deliverable. It publishes the translated languages alongside the English source in a single PDF.

body.p: Repeat the edit-translate-publish cycle as many times as you like: because tracks translation state incrementally, later jobs only retranslate the topics you changed.

p.note: also provides a template project you can use as a starting point for your own translated content. It is set up the same way as this sample: a multilingual book deliverable and DITA keys defined for each language. See Projects for how to create a project from a template.
